title: What That Kosher Symbol Actually Means

scenes.speaker: Maya
scenes.text: Wait. Your cereal box is not an ownership chart.

scenes.speaker: Alex
scenes.text: That little O-U symbol? It means the product meets the Orthodox Union’s kosher standards. That’s the actual claim.

scenes.speaker: Maya
scenes.text: Okay, but what gets checked? Ingredients, equipment, and production. Kosher follows Jewish dietary law. Companies apply for certification, and yes, they pay fees.

scenes.speaker: Alex
scenes.text: You can question the service or its price. But a paid certification does not prove that Jewish people secretly control a company, or an entire industry.

scenes.speaker: Maya
scenes.text: Want to know who owns the business? Look at company records. Want to know what the certification covers? Check the certifier’s rules.

scenes.speaker: Alex
scenes.text: Different questions. Different evidence. A tiny symbol isn’t doing all the jobs the internet gives it.

scenes.speaker: Maya
scenes.text: The label belongs on the box. Not on people.
scenes.on_screen: THE LABEL BELONGS ON THE BOX
scenes.source: Beyond the Myth · Facts, not scapegoats
